questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I liked Bologna as a city (food, culture) - and its size: It is not too big, and it is centered around the university.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I didn't get much information before I arrived. A lot of things were unclear - including when classes started. However, it all worked out when I arrived.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There was a zoom check-in meeting which was helpful. Other than that, I had to figure it out for myself.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: We took over the apartment that someone we knew had stayed in. It was not expensive and located just outside the city walls (anything within the city walls is very central).

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: You should not expect Bologna to be cheaper than Copenhagen. And a lot of students share rooms. We were three friends who shared an apartment - it might be a good idea to join together and look for apartments.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: We had to schedule a zoom check-in session where you had to show your passport and plane-ticket to the camera. It was pretty easy - we got an e-mail about it when we arrived.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You were able to ask questions during the meeting.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Succesful. Registering for classes happens pretty late - you only have to register online for the exams mid-semester. So it is easy to do try out classes and then decide to swap.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't stress too much about deadlines - registration is generally pretty flexible. Check your e-mail and make sure to register in AlmaEsami during the semester.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The academic level was generally not very challenging (at least at the political science department where I took classes).

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: It didn't always seem very academic - generally, the professors want you to state your own thoughts and opinions as well.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Smaller classes, fewer readings, and more 'high-school'-like class participation. Sometimes they didn't even require references in papers.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Social Stratification and Economic Inequality
Public Economics
Italian Pop Cultures
History of Globalization and Crime

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
We made a lot of friends in the Social Stratification class, and the class itself was fine too.
Italian Pop Cultures was a fun way to learn a little about italian music/modern culture.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Overweight luggage on the way home...

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food, drinks, and going out is cheap, but you also tend to do it a lot, so I ended up spending a lot on that.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There weren't a lot of planned activities, but the city is so nice that it is not necessary. People are very welcoming and making friends was easy.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I didn't really check it out because there was so much else to do. But I think there are Erasmus facebook groups with activities, karaoke nights, and trips to Venice etc.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Use the very good train connections and check out other cities nearby (Milan, Florence, Rome, Naples). And go out at night - people are very open and easy to talk to.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: The city is full of great restaurants, bars, and shopping. We also started at a climbing-gym just outside the city which was fun and social.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy. The italian lifestyle is easy to enjoy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: We found it pretty easy to talk to people in class - that is where we made most of our friends. We also became regulars at a few cafes and bars where people were very welcoming.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: You can't expect everything to be scheduled and people to be on time. But generally, the teachers and everyone else don't expect you to be either.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: People being very welcoming - and very social. You live your life outside and people go out a lot which is a lot of fun.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Check out restaurants, bars, and don't be afraid to talk to strangers when going out.
Talk to people in your class.
Take the train to other cities - it is very easy.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Get a bike (I bought one on Facebook Marketplace). Also: If you go there in february, don't expect it to be 25 degrees and sunny...

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The culture, food, and the social experience.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The administrative processes take time. And it isn't always clear what the exam guidelines are (I was told that I couldn't take my exam online, but in the end 12 other people did for instance).

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Great city! Go for the cultural experience - not the academic one. But I would definitely reccomend it!!!

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
